nl.statement: A \(p\)-dimensional discrete-time linear Gaussian snapshot system observed through one unknown common measurement noise. The latent state evolves by \(X_k=V^k(X_0-x^\star)+x^\star\) with one-step transition \(V=\exp(hG)\) for a continuous-time generator \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) and spacing \(h>0\); the initial law is \(X_0\sim\mathcal N(\mu_0,\Sigma)\) with \(\Sigma\succ0\); at each of the four times \(kh\), \(k\in K=\{0,1,2,3\}\), one observes \(Y_k=X_k+\varepsilon_k\), where the measurement errors \(\varepsilon_k\sim\mathcal N(0,E)\) share a single unknown \(E\succ0\), are mutually independent, and are independent of \(X_0\). The observable object is the four-tuple of Gaussian marginal laws of \(Y_0,Y_1,Y_2,Y_3\), equivalently the moments \(m_k=\mathbb E[Y_k]\) and \(C_k=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_k)\); when the noise covariance is supplied, the noise-subtracted levels are \(\widetilde C_k=C_k-E\). The identity \(I_p\) is the order-\(p\) identity matrix. — SUBSTRATE SURVEY (bypass-justified). Searched `../doc/API.md` section index (`grep '^## '`, 40+ sections) plus the cluster roots `Causalean/PO/`, `Causalean/PO/ID/Exact/`, `Causalean/SCM/ID/`, `Causalean/SCM/ID/GraphicalThms/`, `Causalean/SCM/Do/`, `Causalean/Graph/SWIG.lean` for the concept words `linear dynamical system`, `snapshot`, `transition matrix`, `measurement noise`, `state-space`, `matrix exponential`, `Stein`, `Lyapunov`, `congruence`, `Krylov`, `principal logarithm`, `spectral radius`. Result: Causalean's `PO/` world is a potential-outcome bundle over a probability space with treatment/outcome/covariate maps (`POManskiIVSystem`, `POCFBundle`, `Overlap`, `Backdoor`, `Adjustment`, `ATE/DID/DTR/LATE`) and `SCM/` is a DAG/SWIG do-calculus world; NEITHER carries a latent linear flow, a transition matrix, a measurement-error layer, or a destructive unpaired snapshot design. This artifact has no treatment, no intervention, and no graph -- its structural target is the generator \(G\) -- so `POManskiIVSystem`/`SWIGGraph`/`Identifiable` are at the wrong abstraction and are BYPASS-JUSTIFIED. Mathlib-side check (`lean_leansearch`, `Glob` on `.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/**`): `Matrix.PosDef`, `Matrix.PosSemidef`, `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues`, `Matrix.IsHermitian.spectral_theorem`, `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvectorUnitary`, `NormedSpace.exp`/`Matrix.exp_*`, `spectralRadius` all CONFIRMED present; these are the reuse floor. Note `Matrix.PosSemidef.sqrt` is ABSENT in this Mathlib snapshot (grepped `.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/{Analysis,LinearAlgebra}/Matrix/PosDef.lean` for `sqrt` -- only norm-induced hits) -- hence D-plan-2 routes square roots through `Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc`.

The observable moment chart of the four snapshot laws and its whitened congruence geometry. The common noise cancels from the adjacent covariance decreases \(H_j=C_j-C_{j+1}\), \(j\in\{0,1,2\}\), and from the mean probes \(d_j=m_{j+1}-m_j\). Whitening produces the source and target invariants \(R=H_0^{-1/2}H_1H_0^{-1/2}\) and \(S=H_1^{-1/2}H_2H_1^{-1/2}\) with common spectrum \(\Lambda\), orthonormal eigenframes \(P_\lambda\) (for \(R\)) and \(Q_\lambda\) (for \(S\)), block probes \(A_\lambda=P_\lambda^{\mathsf T}H_0^{-1/2}[d_0,d_1]\) and \(B_\lambda=Q_\lambda^{\mathsf T}H_1^{-1/2}[d_1,d_2]\), multiplicities \(m_\lambda\), probe ranks \(r_\lambda=\operatorname{rank}A_\lambda\), residual dimensions \(k_\lambda=m_\lambda-r_\lambda\), block isometries \(O_\lambda\in O(m_\lambda)\) with \(O_\lambda A_\lambda=B_\lambda\), and the binary-block count \(q=\#\{\lambda:k_\lambda=1\}\). A candidate transition \(W\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) ranges over the raw fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\), the admissible fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\), the three-snapshot fiber \(\mathcal F_3\), and the supplied-noise fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\). Each candidate carries the Stein operator \(\mathcal L_W(A)=A-WAW^{\mathsf T}\) with reconstruction \(T_W\) solving \(T_W-WT_WW^{\mathsf T}=H_0\), the recovered noise \(E_W=C_0-T_W\), the principal-logarithm generator \(G_W=h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}W\), the equilibrium \(x_W^\star=(I_p-W)^{-1}(m_1-Wm_0)\), and the full reconstruction \(\theta(W,z)\) of the moment stack \(z=(m_0,\ldots,m_3,\operatorname{vech}C_0,\ldots,\operatorname{vech}C_3)\). The rational chart is generated by \(M_0=H_1H_0^{-1}\), \(M_1=H_2H_1^{-1}\), the Krylov matrices \(K_i=[d_i,M_id_i,\ldots,M_i^{p-1}d_i]\), and the recovery map \(\mathcal K=K_1K_0^{-1}\). The off-model criterion is the residual map \(F_{\mathrm{res}}(W;z)\), with derivative \(D_WF\) and regularity margin \(\gamma_W=\sigma_{\min}(D_WF)\). — SUBSTRATE SURVEY (bypass-justified for Causalean causal modules; genuine Mathlib reuse). Grepped `../doc/API.md` and `Glob`ed `Causalean/**` for `whitening`, `congruence`, `orthogonal torsor`, `stabilizer`, `eigenspace block`, `Krylov`, `Stein equation`, `matrix logarithm`. Nothing in `Causalean/PO/`, `Causalean/SCM/`, or `Causalean/Graph/` speaks about matrix congruence orbits; `Causalean/Stat/Concentration/Matrix/{Resolvent,InversePerturbation,DesignInverse,IidSums}.lean` is the only matrix-analysis corner and it is an l-infinity-operator-norm inverse-perturbation toolbox (see S3), not congruence geometry -- BYPASS-JUSTIFIED for the geometry, REUSED for the perturbation. Mathlib-side check CONFIRMED: `Matrix.orthogonalGroup` (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/UnitaryGroup.lean`), `Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc` + `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvectorUnitary` + `Matrix.IsHermitian.spectral_theorem` (`Mathlib/Analysis/Matrix/{HermitianFunctionalCalculus,Spectrum}.lean`), `Matrix.kroneckerMap` (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Kronecker.lean`), `Matrix.det_vandermonde` (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Vandermonde.lean`, needed for the `det K_0 != 0` genericity witness in `thm:snapshot-frontier`). ABSENT in Mathlib and build-inline here: any discrete Lyapunov/Stein solution operator, and any principal matrix logarithm for a non-normal matrix (`CFC.log` is restricted to self-adjoint / strictly-positive elements -- verified via `lean_leansearch` 'principal matrix logarithm ... spectrum avoids the nonpositive reals').

The deterministic moment-perturbation regime on the cyclic chart. Each observed mean and covariance coordinate is perturbed by at most \(\epsilon\) (Euclidean norm for means, operator norm for covariances). The population instance supplies the covariance margin \(a_0=\min\{\lambda_{\min}(H_0),\lambda_{\min}(H_1)\}\), the scales \(B_{\mathrm{norm}}=\max\{1,\lVert H_0\rVert,\lVert H_1\rVert,\lVert H_2\rVert\}\) and \(D_{\mathrm{norm}}=\max\{1,\lVert d_0\rVert,\lVert d_1\rVert\}\), the quotient constant \(c_M=4/a_0+4B_{\mathrm{norm}}/a_0^2\), the power scale \(L_M=1+\max\{1,\lVert M_0\rVert,\lVert M_1\rVert\}\), the Krylov constant \(c_K=\sqrt p\max_{0\le j<p}\{2L_M^j+jL_M^{j-1}c_MD_{\mathrm{norm}}\}\), the cyclicity margin \(\kappa=\sigma_{\min}(K_0)\), the transition constant \(c_V=2c_K(1+\lVert V\rVert)/\kappa\), the stability and logarithm-cut radii \(\delta_{\mathrm{stab}},\delta_{\log}\), the Stein margin \(\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}=\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal L_V)\), the reconstruction margins \(t_{\min}=\lambda_{\min}(T_V)\) and \(e_{\min}=\lambda_{\min}(E_V)\), the propagation constants \(c_T=2\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}[2\sqrt p+c_V(2\lVert V\rVert+1)\lVert T_V\rVert_F]\) and \(c_E=1+c_T\), and the two admissibility radii \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\). — REUSE (analogous-module, technique-level). Searched `Causalean/Stat/Concentration/Matrix/` (`Glob Causalean/Stat/**/*.lean`, then `lean_file_outline`): `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.designInv_perturb` proves `IsUnit S.det -> row-sum bound on S-inverse -> entrywise closeness -> IsUnit M.det /\ |M-inv - S-inv| <= 2 c^2 (p+1) eta`, i.e. exactly the Neumann-series inverse-perturbation pattern the paper uses for `H_i^{-1}` and `K_0^{-1}`. It is stated in l-infinity operator norm with entrywise inputs, while `thm:cyclic-perturbation` needs spectral/operator norm with `sigma_min` inputs -- GAP TO BRIDGE: re-run the same Neumann factorization at operator norm using `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Matrix.Resolvent` + `Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Normed`. F3 should adapt `Causalean/Stat/Concentration/Matrix/InversePerturbation.lean:112 designInv_perturb` rather than rebuild. Mathlib-side check: `lean_leansearch` 'discrete Lyapunov Stein equation unique solution spectral radius less than one' returns only `spectralRadius` API (`Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Algebra/{Spectrum,GelfandFormula}.lean`) -- no Stein-operator invertibility lemma exists, so the `sigma_Stein` leg is build-inline.

The destructive-snapshot sampling experiment and its branchwise inference. At each time \(kh\), \(n_k\) independent units are drawn from the marginal law of \(Y_k\), independently across \(k\); no unit is followed across time. Writing \(N=\sum_{k=0}^3 n_k\), the limiting shares satisfy \(n_k/N\to\pi_k\in(0,1)\). Sample means and sample covariances form the empirical moment stack \(\widehat z\), whose rescaled deviation \(\sqrt N(\widehat z-z)\) has Gaussian limit covariance \(\Omega\). On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat K_i=[\widehat d_i,\widehat M_i\widehat d_i,\ldots,\widehat M_i^{p-1}\widehat d_i]\) give the plug-in transition \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\), with reconstructions \(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}\), \(\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) and full parameter \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\). On a specified regular finite branch, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is the global residual minimizer over a fixed population-centered ball, with plug-in \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{loc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\) and delta-method Jacobian \(J_\theta\). Simultaneous statements are indexed by a nominal error probability \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). The certified branch handle \(\text{CertHandle}\) is the starting move for the open construction problem of locating and labelling every empirical branch. — REUSE (strong). Searched `Causalean/Stat/{CLT,Limit,Inference,MEstimation}/` for `multivariate CLT`, `delta method`, `asymptotic linearity`, `argmin stability`, `Z-estimator`. CONFIRMED reusable at proof-step level: `Causalean.Stat.deltaMethod` (`Stat/Inference/DeltaMethod.lean:279`, multivariate Frechet-derivative delta method at the ProbabilityMeasure level, `HasFDerivAt g Dg t0` + weak convergence -> pushforward `Q.map Dg`) is the exact engine for `sqrt N (theta-hat_loc - theta(W,z)) ==> N(0, J Omega J^T)`; `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample.clt_normalizedSum_vec` (`Stat/CLT/MultivariateCLT.lean:120`) + `Causalean.Stat.gaussianLimit` (`Stat/CLT/GaussianLimit.lean:63`, with `gaussianLimit_charFun`, `gaussianLimit_covarianceBilin`) supply the vector i.i.d. CLT and its concrete centered Gaussian limit; `Tendsto_dist_vec` lives in `Stat/Limit/ConvergenceVec.lean`. GAP TO BRIDGE: the paper's design is FOUR independent samples of sizes `n_k` with `n_k/N -> pi_k`, not one `IIDSample`, so F3 must combine four applications of `clt_normalizedSum_vec` through independence + the share limits (characteristic-function product, as in the frozen proof) rather than instantiate a single `IIDSample`. `Causalean.Stat.MEstimation.{ArgmaxStability,ZEstimator}` carry the contraction/argmin-uniqueness pattern for the fixed-ball global-minimizer step. BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: `Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/` (Stein / dependency-graph CLT, `wald_coverage`) is design-based with treatment assignment as the only randomness -- wrong randomness model here, where sampling is i.i.d. from four fixed Gaussian marginals.
The state dimension satisfies \(p\ge 2\).

nl.statement: \[\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}=\{W\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}:WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1,\ WH_1W^{\mathsf T}=H_2,\ Wd_0=d_1,\ Wd_1=d_2\}.\]
\[\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}=\{W\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}:\rho(W)<1,\ \operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing,\ E_W\succ0\}.\]

For a supplied \(E\), set \(\widetilde C_k=C_k-E\) and define \[\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)=\left\{W\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}:\begin{array}{l}\widetilde C_k\succ0\text{ for }k\in K,\quad W\widetilde C_kW^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_{k+1}\text{ for }k=0,1,2,\\ Wd_0=d_1,\quad Wd_1=d_2,\quad \rho(W)<1,\quad \operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing,\\ E_W=E\quad\text{equivalently}\quad C_0-E-T_W=0\end{array}\right\}.\]
\[\mathcal F_{3}=\{W\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}:WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1,\ Wd_0=d_1\}.\]
\[\mathcal K((m_k),(C_k))=K_1K_0^{-1},\qquad K_i=[d_i,M_id_i,\ldots,M_i^{p-1}d_i],\quad M_i=H_{i+1}H_i^{-1}.\]

Let \(\widehat m_k\) and \(\widehat C_k\) denote the moment coordinates of \(\widehat z\). For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), set \(\widehat d_i=\widehat m_{i+1}-\widehat m_i\), \(\widehat M_i=(\widehat C_{i+1}-\widehat C_{i+2})(\widehat C_i-\widehat C_{i+1})^{-1}\), and \(\widehat K_i=[\widehat d_i,\widehat M_i\widehat d_i,\ldots,\widehat M_i^{p-1}\widehat d_i]\). Whenever the displayed inverses exist, define \[\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}.\]
\[F_{\mathrm{res}}(W;z)=\bigl(\operatorname{vech}(WH_0W^{\mathsf T}-H_1),\operatorname{vech}(WH_1W^{\mathsf T}-H_2),Wd_0-d_1,Wd_1-d_2\bigr).\]

Fix a population raw branch \(W\) and a radius \(r>0\) such that the closed Frobenius ball \(\mathcal B_r(W)=\{U:\lVert U-W\rVert_F\leq r\}\) contains no other zero of \(F_{\mathrm{res}}(\,cdot\,;z)\).  For a moment vector \(\zeta\), whenever
\[
 \underset{U\in\mathcal B_r(W)}{\operatorname{argmin}}\,
 \lVert F_{\mathrm{res}}(U;\zeta)\rVert_2^2
\]
is a singleton, define \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}(\zeta)\) to be its unique element.  Define a total measurable completion by taking the unique argmin when it is a singleton and assigning the fixed population-indexed fallback \(W\) otherwise.  Any measurable completion agreeing with the unique argmin on its singleton region is denoted \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\).

For a transition \(U\) and a moment vector \(\zeta\) with coordinates \(m_k(\zeta)\) and \(C_k(\zeta)\), let \(T(U;\zeta)\) solve \(T-UTU^{\mathsf T}=C_0(\zeta)-C_1(\zeta)\), and define \[\theta(U,\zeta)=\bigl(\operatorname{vec}U,\operatorname{vec}(h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}U),\operatorname{vech}T(U;\zeta),\operatorname{vech}(C_0(\zeta)-T(U;\zeta)),(I_p-U)^{-1}(m_1(\zeta)-Um_0(\zeta)),m_0(\zeta)\bigr).\] Thus the last coordinate reconstructs \(\mu_0=m_0(\zeta)\).

Eliminate the block-orthogonal completion variables from the covariance and mean residual equations into a zero-dimensional polynomial system on each finite stratum; use Smale \(\alpha\)-quantities to target certified real roots, and use interval enclosures for stability, the principal-logarithm cut, the Stein solve, and strict \(E_W\)-positivity.

The raw fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\) is nonempty if and only if \(R\) and \(S\) have identical eigenvalues with identical multiplicities and \(A_\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_\lambda=B_\lambda^{\mathsf T}B_\lambda\) for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\). When these conditions hold, every member appears exactly once as \[W=H_1^{1/2}\left(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}Q_\lambda O_\lambda P_\lambda^{\mathsf T}\right)H_0^{-1/2},\qquad O_\lambda A_\lambda=B_\lambda,\quad O_\lambda\in O(m_\lambda),\] where the completion fiber of block \(\lambda\) is a torsor for \(O(k_\lambda)\) and has dimension \(k_\lambda(k_\lambda-1)/2\).

The map \(W\mapsto\theta(W,z)\), whose last coordinate is \(\mu_0=m_0\), is a bijection from \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\) to all structural explanations of the four observed Gaussian snapshot laws. Equivalently, a raw candidate is compatible if and only if \(\rho(W)<1\), \(\operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing\), and the Stein reconstruction satisfies \(E_W=C_0-T_W\succ0\). Global identification holds if and only if \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is a singleton.

For model-compatible three-snapshot laws, the exact dimension-dependent frontier is as follows.  If \(p=2\) and \(d_0
e0\), the two raw \(O(1)\) completions have opposite determinants, the negative-determinant completion fails the principal-logarithm cut, and the admissible transition and full structural explanation are unique.  If \(p=2\) and \(d_0=0\), a continuous local \(O(2)\) ambiguity remains.  If \(p\ge3\), every model-compatible law has continuous local ambiguity: its dimension is \((p-1)(p-2)/2\) when \(d_0
e0\) and \(p(p-1)/2\) when \(d_0=0\).  The condition \(d_0
e0\) is generic in the mean parameter.  With four snapshots, \(\det K_0
e0\) implies the rational recovery identity \(V=K_1K_0^{-1}\), and \(\det K_0
e0\) holds outside a proper algebraic subset of the admissible parameter domain.  Thus three snapshots generically identify the full explanation when \(p=2\); a fourth snapshot is generically necessary when \(p\ge3\) and is generically sufficient on the cyclic chart whenever the recovered candidate passes the admissibility filters.

At every compatible explanation, \[\dim\ker(D_WF)=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\frac{k_\lambda(k_\lambda-1)}{2}.\] The derivative of the full Gaussian parameter-to-moment map has the same kernel after the Stein, measurement-covariance, equilibrium, and initial-mean coordinates are included. Consequently the branchwise Fisher information is nonsingular exactly on the finite raw strata \(k_\lambda\le1\) for all \(\lambda\). The Fisher-information claim is for the destructive-snapshot experiment with independent samples drawn separately from the four marginal laws.

On the cyclic chart \(\det K_0\ne0\), suppose every mean and covariance coordinate of \(\widehat z\) differs from its population counterpart by at most \(\epsilon\) in Euclidean or operator norm, respectively. If \(\epsilon\le\min\{a_0/4,1/c_M,\kappa/(2c_K)\}\), then \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) is defined and \(\lVert\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}-V\rVert\le c_V\epsilon\). If in addition \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\), then \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) remains stable and off the principal-logarithm cut, its Stein operator is invertible, and every coordinate of the full plug-in \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\) is defined. If \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\), then \(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}\succ0\) and \(\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}\succ0\), so every dynamical, logarithm, Stein, and covariance-positivity admissibility filter is preserved. Quantitatively, \(\lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert\le c_T\epsilon\) and \(\lVert\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}-E_V\rVert\le c_E\epsilon\), and the principal logarithm, equilibrium, and initial-mean coordinates obey linear bounds determined by their resolvent, \(\lVert(I_p-V)^{-1}\rVert\), and the moment error. These domain conclusions concern the reconstruction from perturbed moments; they do not assert the exact population raw equalities for \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}\).

Fix a finite raw branch \(W\) with \(\gamma_W>0\), strict admissibility margins, and a ball containing no other raw branch. Choose any measurable total completion from \(\text{def:local-branch-estimator}\). On a sufficiently small neighborhood of the population moment \(z\), the branch-local residual estimator \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\), defined as the unique global minimizer over that fixed ball, is a smooth off-model extension. Under independent Gaussian snapshot sampling its full moment plug-in \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{loc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\), including the initial-mean coordinate \(\widehat\mu_0=\widehat m_0\), satisfies \[\sqrt N\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{loc}}-\theta(W,z)\bigr)\;\Longrightarrow\;\mathcal N(0,J_\theta\Omega J_\theta^{\mathsf T}).\] Replacing population moments and the recovered local branch in \(J_\theta\Omega J_\theta^{\mathsf T}\) yields a consistent branchwise covariance estimator.

Suppose that the common measurement covariance \(E\) is supplied, and set \(\widetilde C_k=C_k-E\).  Within the present stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise structural model, the transition fiber compatible with the four observed marginal laws is exactly \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\).  Its covariance restrictions are \(W\widetilde C_kW^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_{k+1}\) for \(k=0,1,2\), and its residual-noise restriction is the equality \(E_W=E\), equivalently \(C_0-E-T_W=0\), rather than only the unknown-noise inequality \(C_0-T_W\succ0\).  With only snapshots \(k=0,1,2\), the covariance and affine-mean consequences are exactly \(W\widetilde C_0W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_1\), \(W\widetilde C_1W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_2\), and \(Wd_0=d_1\).  Under the identification of the published discrete transition with \(W\), its state covariances with \(\widetilde C_k\), and its known process covariance with \(Q=0\), these are an equation-level subclass of AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1.  The inclusion is strict at model scope: their full-state system permits a known nonzero process covariance, an invertible discrete-time transition without stability or continuous-time embeddability restrictions, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws, whereas it has no measurement-error layer.  Thus only the displayed moment-equation consequence, not equality of observation-model classes, is inherited.  If the two three-snapshot whitened congruence invariants have the same simple spectrum and every source probe coordinate is nonzero, the three-snapshot equations are computably reduced to at most \(2^p\) sign candidates.  The candidates for \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\) are then tested against the remaining fourth-snapshot congruence and probe equation and against the stability, principal-logarithm, Stein, and equality \(E_W=E\) filters.

Can \(\text{CertHandle}\) be completed into an output-sensitive, data-based initializer and canonical labeling rule which, on every regular noncyclic finite stratum, returns disjoint certified neighborhoods containing all and only admissible branches exactly once, remains unchanged under perturbations smaller than an explicit separation margin from every excluded branch, and supports simultaneous branchwise confidence regions with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\)?

Assume \(p\ge 2\) and \(H_0,H_1\succ0\).  The three-snapshot raw fiber \(\mathcal F_3\) is nonempty if and only if
\[
 \lVert H_0^{-1/2}d_0\rVert_2=\lVert H_1^{-1/2}d_1\rVert_2.
\]
When this equality holds, put \(r=\operatorname{rank}(H_0^{-1/2}d_0)\in\{0,1\}\).  Under the bijection
\[
 U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2},
\]
the raw fiber is noncanonically a torsor for \(O(p-r)\), and its dimension is
\[
 \frac{(p-r)(p-r-1)}{2}.
\]
Its intersection with the strict filter set
\[
 \left\{W:\rho(W)<1,\ \operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing,\ C_0-T_W\succ0\right\}
\]
is exactly the transition identified set for the three observed Gaussian snapshot laws and is relatively open in \(\mathcal F_3\).  Consequently every nonempty local admissible branch has the displayed dimension.  If \(d_0\ne0\) and \(p\ge3\), this dimension is positive.  If \(p=2\) and \(d_0\ne0\), the raw fiber consists of exactly two candidates with opposite determinants.  A real matrix with negative determinant has a negative real eigenvalue, so at most one of these candidates passes the principal-logarithm cut; for model-compatible observed laws exactly one passes all three filters, and the full structural explanation is identified.  This is the generic mean regime in dimension two.  If \(d_0=0\), nonemptiness is equivalent to \(d_1=0\), the raw fiber is a torsor for \(O(p)\), and continuous ambiguity occurs already at \(p=2\).  The continuous nonidentification conclusions for \(p\ge3\), and for \(d_0=0\) when \(p=2\), transfer to every unknown-common-measurement-covariance model whose model class contains the present stable, embeddable, deterministic Gaussian class as a subclass and has the same transition target.

Section 2 of AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 studies, in a locally denoted dimension \(n\), the exactly observed full-state recursion \(Z_j=A Z_{j-1}+b+\eta_{j-1}\), where the process innovations have known covariance \(Q\) and the temporal orthogonality specified there.  Its moment equations are \(\bar m_j=A\bar m_{j-1}+b\) and \(P_j=AP_{j-1}A^{\mathsf T}+Q\).  Theorem 2.1 assumes that \(A\) is invertible but imposes neither stability nor continuous-time embeddability, and the paragraph immediately following its proof states that finite second moments, rather than Gaussianity, suffice for these moment equations and the stated identification argument.

Whenever the raw four-snapshot fiber is nonempty, it is finite if and only if \(k_\lambda\leq 1\) for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\); on a finite stratum it contains exactly \(2^q\) candidates before admissibility filtering.  If some \(k_\lambda\geq 2\), every admissible candidate lies in a positive-dimensional relatively open fiber.  On a finite stratum with \(q\geq1\), at most \(2^{q-1}\) raw candidates are admissible, while for \(q=0\) at most one is admissible.  Consequently, in dimension \(p\geq2\), every finite admissible fiber has at most \(2^{p-1}\) members.  This bound is sharp: for every \(p\geq2\), there are strict-decrease Gaussian snapshot laws for which \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\) has \(2^p\) members and \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\), and hence the compatible structural-explanation fiber, has exactly \(2^{p-1}\) members.
